News.title: Incredible moment Ukrainian troops use robot to save OAP, 77, from ‘grey zone’ under relentless Russian shelling
News.content:
NAN-DROID TO RESCUE Incredible moment Ukrainian troops use robot to save OAP, 77, from ‘grey zone’ under relentless Russian shelling

A LONE civilian was dramatically saved by a robot after being spotted walking through a shattered “grey zone” under relentless Russian shelling.

The 77-year-old woman had almost no chance of survival as she trudged along the bullet-riddled road surrounded by craters and bodies of fellow villagers.





Heading toward the Lyman direction, the elderly citizen was completely exposed in an active combat zone.

Drone operators from Ukraine’s 60th Mechanised Brigade spotted her from above – triggering a high-risk rescue mission as explosions continued around her.

In a staggering four-hour operation, troops deployed an unmanned ground robot, sending it rolling through the frontline to reach her.



To avoid frightening her, fighters covered it with a blanket and left a message: “Grandma, get on!” – and incredibly she did.

She was carried to safety while three more civillians were guided out by drones, after her home of 53 years was destroyed by Russian forces.

It comes after it was alleged that Vladimir Putin’s soldiers are turning to cannibalism after running low on provisions during the deep winter.

Intercepted audio communications between Russian officers and photos point to “starvation” on the frontline in Ukraine, forcing comrades to eat each other.



A Ukrainian intelligence source said they had evidence of at least five such incidents, The Sunday Times reported.

Among the most disturbing incidents reportedly happened in November 2025 near the town of Myrnohrad in Donetsk region.

A Russian soldier referred to by his call sign Khromoy, meaning “limpy”, was caught after killing two comrades and attempting to eat the leg of one of them.

He is understood to have been serving with the 95th regiment of the 5th Separate Guards Motor Rifle Brigade.

News.title: Four killed and dozens injured after two trains crash into each other on the same track as passengers left ‘screaming’
News.content:
RAIL SMASH Four killed and dozens injured after two trains crash into each other on the same track as passengers left ‘screaming’

TWO trains have smashed into each other outside the Indonesian capital of Jakarta killing at least four people and trapping dozens more.

It’s understood one train slammed into another which was stationary, causing massive destruction to both.





Rescue teams are working desperately to reach at least five passengers still trapped in the mangled commuter train car.

Authorities fear the death toll could increase.

Passengers could be heard screamed hysterically as the trains collided, one passenger told the BBC.

Other eyewitnesses said they had seen “many victims” injured in the crash.



Some 38 passengers were taken to hospitals for treatment, state-owned railway company PT Kereta Api Indonesia said in a statement.

The Argo Bromo Anggrek long-distance train crashed into the rear car of a commuter train that was stopped at Bekasi Timur Station.



The car had been designated for women only, a common accommodation to help avoid harassment.

All 240 passengers on the Argo Bromo Anggrek train were safe, officials said.

Police were investigating the cause of the accident, Jakarta Police Chief Asep Edi Suheri told reporters at the scene.



Local television footage and videos on social media showed passengers at the station panicking, while dozens of people rushed to the station for news of family members.

News.title: Police officer facing the sack over shocking ‘Harvey Price jibes and racist messages in WhatsApps to former cop’
News.content:
HARVEY 'JIBE' Police officer facing the sack over shocking ‘Harvey Price jibes and racist messages in WhatsApps to former cop’

A COP faces the sack for referring to new recruits as ­“Harveys who need to be read to” in a reference to Katie Price’s disabled son, a disciplinary hearing was told.

Trainer Police Sergeant Natalie Dolan included the offensive remark in a WhatsApp to a former cop identified only as PC Jones, it was said.





The “ableist” dig was among racist, sexist and offensive ­messages experienced Greater Manchester Police (GMP) cop Dolan is accused of sending.

Counsel for GMP, Stephen Morley, said the reference to Harvey suggested “the student officers have learning difficulties because they need to be read to like Harvey Price”.

Mr Morley added: “That is ­discriminatory to Harvey Price and also to the student officers it is referring to. That is mocking of the disability and mocking of the student officers.”

Harvey, 23, has rare genetic disorder Prader-Willi syndrome, autism and is partially-sighted.

Mr Morley said Sgt Dolan, 48, also sent a racist message which read: “Blame HR for recruiting at the mosque.”

He told the hearing: “Sgt Dolan is suggesting that recruiting at the mosque will get you less able candidates.”

There was also mention of a “licker” which Mr Morley said referred to a disabled person licking a window.

The messages, sent from May 2021 to February 2022, came to light in a criminal probe by GMP’s professional standards.



At the time, Sgt Dolan — praised for her work in a ­former police role — had been a cop for around 20 years.

Mr Morley said her words were “inappropriate” for an officer “training student officers and leading by example”.

He said: “The messages are not only offensive but discriminatory, racist and ableist.”

He went on: “She must have realised what she was doing was totally unacceptable. But she carried on doing it.”

Sgt Dolan is also accused of sharing confidential information about other cops with former PC Jones and failing to declare a conflict of interest in relation to her former colleague.



The ongoing hearing, at GMP’s Manchester HQ, was told her messages breached professional standards and amounted to gross misconduct.

News.title: Only way to get to bottom of I’m A Celeb bullying row is for ITV to share unedited footage – but I know why they won’t
News.content:
HAVE ITV finally cracked the code to saving linear TV?

Friday night’s dynamite live I’m A Celeb final was EVERYTHING you could ever want from a piece of television.





There was jeopardy, in-fighting, Gemma Collins dressed as The Grinch, Sinitta marching off set unable to get a word in edgeways, and general unmitigated chaos.

With viewers deserting traditional telly in their droves, ditching glossy-floored game shows and plodding police procedurals for social media — where the action is in real time, featuring real, flawed people — is more live TV what we actually need?

It was, then, so contrary to Adam’s foul-mouthed, C-word-heavy rant in South Africa, which was neatly edited and repackaged to be more palatable for Emmerdale fans.

In a world of Instagram filters and carefully curated stories, how refreshing then to have some livewires tearing up the stage. Finally, a real water cooler moment! The action was supremely presided over by the unflappable Ant and Dec.

In so doing, the duo finally showed us why ITV insist on endlessly giving them £40million golden handcuff deals.

So, of course, what are ITV doing now? Scrapping the show.

Now, loads has been written about the whole David Haye/Jimmy Bullard vs Adam Thomas fallout.

As David told me last week, “One person’s banter is another’s bullying.”





Jimmy and David’s biggest problem was criticising the show whilst they were on the show.

Ant and Dec’s very livelihood depends on protecting their ITV paymasters.

They weren’t going to throw the network to the lions now.

“I was there and didn’t find it abusive,” said Ant. Seconds after stating the jungle rant was, in fact, “unbroadcastable”.

So who was right?

Well there’s only one way to answer that: ITV must release the unedited footage, hurty words bleeped out. But of course they won’t.

Because they have a vested interest in protecting Adam, a far more marketable star whose agent is ITV exec Kevin Lygo’s daughter and whose brother, Ryan, is a former Corrie stalwart.

Whatever your take, though, the resultant outcry has shown just how soft we’ve become as a nation.

FIRED UP ON TIKTOK

AND to think we all thought there was only one raging narcissist in the White House.



Saturday night’s assassination attempt on President Trump – the third in two years – was awful.

But not even the big orange man himself, as he was being whisked to safety by a swarm of Hollywood-esque, gun-toting Secret Service agents, thought to stop, whip out his smartphone, and record the moment for posterity. Or TikTok.

No, that was left to a legion of Gen Z reporters in attendance at the annual media event.

Footage has gone viral of young, thirsty reporters all filming themselves diving under tables.

Brave new world… or vain new world?

MEME OF THE WEEK

KYLIE Jenner, below, has posed gormlessly in front of her collection of Hermes bags, reportedly worth £1.7million.

Not discounting the number of crocodiles, lambs and kangaroos killed for this haul, such a display of wealth is absolutely grotesque.

Included in her Instagram “carousel” was a photo taken inside her private jet.



At the risk of sounding all Jeremy Corbyn, NO ONE needs this much money.

MANDY POOS IN BRIEFS

WHILST it’s not easy to find sympathy with Peter Mandelson, he has had a hat-trick of most unfortunate photographs made very, very public.

Ones that no Instagram filter in the world could make better.

First we had him snapped in his saggy white underpants, grimly exposed in the Epstein files.

Then we had our fallen Dark Lord caught short, and pictured urinating on a posh London street.

And now poor Mandy has been papped picking up dog poo.

An unhappy treble.

News.title: My sister’s husband ‘confessed’ to strangling her but walked FREE – will shock twist 34yrs on finally bring us justice?
News.content:
FOR 34 years, Keith Hall has denied killing his wife Patricia – despite a honeytrap “confession” to an undercover cop.

Now the past is coming back to haunt him as officials re-examine the mum of two’s mysterious disappearance.





In an extraordinarily rare move, a coroner will open an inquest into the fate of Avon lady Patricia despite her body never being found.

When The Sun approached Keith this week to ask about the inquest, he aggressively shouted at our reporter: “Go away, go away. You’re not wanted.”

He is expected to be called to the hearing, along with police officers who investigated Patricia’s disappearance at the time.

It comes after years of campaigning from Patricia’s sister Christine Weatherhead, who firmly believes her sister was murdered and wants her death acknowledged.

Ex-nurse Christine, 64, said: “Patricia would have never left her children. I want her death to be officially recognised. She’s not an invisible woman, a case number of an unsolved crime file.

“She was a brilliant sister, a devoted mum and a vibrant, fun-loving woman loved by so many.”

‘Miss her every day’

Patricia was 39 when she vanished without trace after a stormy row with her husband Keith, then 38, on January 27, 1992, at their semi-detached home in Pudsey, Leeds.





Bread delivery man Keith was eventually charged with her murder after he confessed to an undercover police officer known as Liz, who had found him through a lonely hearts column.

Having fallen in love with her, Keith told Liz: “I strangled her but it wasn’t that easy’.

He then revealed he had dropped Patricia’s body into an incinerator.

Keith has always maintained he told Liz that he strangled Patricia as he was in love with her and would have said anything to keep her.

He says his wife actually drove off in the family car, which was later found abandoned nearby.

The secretly taped confession was ruled inadmissible as evidence by a Leeds Crown Court judge at Keith’s nine-day trial in February 1994 and he was found not guilty by a majority verdict.

It was alleged Keith killed Patricia as he feared losing his home, business and children as she was planning to leave him.

On the day he walked free from court, the judge agreed to an application by several media organisations to release the honeytrap tapes to the public.

I want her death to be officially recognised. She’s not an invisible woman, a case number of an unsolved crime file Christine Weatherhead, Patricia’s sister

The case attracted national attention, raising questions about police methods. Since then, Patricia has been classed as a missing person and the case has remained open.

But her family are convinced she would never have left behind her two boys, Andrew, then nine, and Graeme, five.



Christine wept as she told The Sun: “For me, an inquest will help bring some closure.

“I cannot accept that Patricia remains a missing person when she has never contacted me or her lads.

“She never took her passport or accessed her bank account. Only a fool would believe she was still alive, so for me it is important to have it on record that she is dead and who was responsible for that.

“I miss her every day but an inquest will give respect and dignity to Pat as she will be declared dead and officially recognised.

“I find it hard to believe it is going to happen after suffering so many setbacks.

“At last, justice is finally supporting Pat and myself. We will be given a voice.”

Christine, of Galphay, North Yorks, has spent more than three decades fighting for Patricia to be officially declared dead.



I strangled her but it wasn’t that easy Keith Hall

The married grandmother first applied for an inquest in 1994 with the support of then West Yorkshire Senior Coroner David Hinchliff.

But Michael Howard, who was Home Secretary at the time, refused on the basis she might still be alive and it would not be right for an inquest to offer a contradictory finding to one in a criminal court.

He said a hearing could be seen as having “potential for unfairness to an acquitted defendant”.

‘Game of life’

Christine was unsuccessful in challenging the ruling in a Judicial Review. She wanted to take the fight to the Court of Appeal but could not get legal aid.

Christine reapplied for an inquest last year, arguing that her sister could no longer be alive.

The case was referred to the Chief Coroner for England and Wales. Within 48 hours, her wish was finally granted.

Christine said: “It has been a long journey to get to this point.

“I cried when I was told an inquest had been ordered. I felt as if finally someone was listening to me.”

It comes after a two-year review of the cold case by West Yorkshire police.

Christine says police told her Patricia was being treated as a homicide victim, not a missing person.”



After Patricia’s death, her sister learned that Keith had started divorce proceedings at Durham court in 2001 and was granted a decree nisi at Leeds in October that year.

As Keith was no longer Patricia’s next of kin, a life insurance policy taken out by her with Allied Dunbar was paid in 2006 to her sons. It is believed they received a total of over £160,000.

Before she vanished, Patricia allegedly told her sister-in-law that Keith had tried to strangle her.

The case was the subject of Amazon documentary The Confession in which Keith denied he had ever hurt his wife.

He said: “It never happened. And the police said, ‘Is this other person lying?’.

“There was only one person that was making up the story and that was Patricia, I’m afraid.”

He went on to tell producers: “We’re all players in a game of life. It’s how we play the hand we’re dealt that’s important.”

News.title: How delicious to see floundering Russell Brand and his performative Christianity so expertly demolished by Piers Morgan
News.content:
FOR any would-be journalists out there, Piers Morgan gave a one-man masterclass in letting a wrong’un hang himself.

The broadcaster’s interview with Russell Brand – a man facing trial on three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault against six women spanning a ten year period – was deliciously excruciating.





To be clear, and from personal experience, there is absolutely nothing delicious about crucifix-wearing Brand.

But Piers single-handedly demolished a man who thinks big words make him smarter than the rest of us.

Today Brand is an evangelical born-again Christian. He has repented and is very, very sorry. Nothing to see here, M’Lord.

Baptised in the Thames by TV’s Bear Grylls in 2024, Brand – who, for years, paid a publicist three grand a month to bolster his image – is relying now on God to do his PR.

During the Uncensored show interview on YouTube, Brand, who asked Piers to perform a pre-show prayer, above, was seen clutching the bible he took into court two months ago.

Asked by the presenter to read out his favourite passage, for 100 painful seconds, Brand haplessly flicked through Ecclesiastes trying to find it.

Piers, for once, was silent. Letting Brand scrabble and flounder, no big words ready to save him.

No act of God, sadly, either.





Instead, how performative we now know Russell’s Christianity to be. (Plus, in the age of the smartphone, he could simply Google some Bible, should the urge strike).

Like a skinny jean-wearing, waxed chest-exposing magician, for decades this “comedian” has used distraction as his greatest weapon.

Finally now we all see his new-found religion for what it really is: smoke and mirrors.

A licence to be forgiven so he can grift some more.

Like his florid monologues and quasi-spiritual jargon, Brand is a washed-up act trying to seduce with his pseudo-intellect while ruthlessly tormenting those he’s wronged.

News.title: Greens says lunchtime pint is bad but heroin is OK… visions of their Marxist dystopia is enough to drive us all to drink
News.content:
NOBODY likes a grass.

But this universal truth didn’t stop the Green Party’s box-fresh MP, Hannah Spencer, dobbing in her fellow Parliamentarians for having the audacity to enjoy the odd bevvy.





After only three months in office, democracy’s latest fruit loop decided to complain that she felt “really uneasy” about her colleagues squeezing a snifter in between late-night votes.

You could “smell the alcohol” in the House she whinged, feigning shock about this “unprofessional and worrying” situation that she reckons never happens in any other profession.

She then confidently claimed that all this casual boozing was causing “questionable and dangerous behaviour” by MPs.

Of course, squealer Spencer didn’t actually speak directly to her allegedly p****d-up colleagues by raising the matter in the Commons (where she has given only ONE speech since she got her vegan sandals under the desk).



No, she preferred the relative safety of a cosy chat in a lefty online echo chamber.

The joyless sanctimony was breathtaking.

Smug Spencer has outed herself as the Commons’ snitch.

You can only imagine what she was like at school . . .



“Miss! Miss! Those boys are talking . . .

“Miss! Miss! Colin’s just flicking the Vs!”

Oh shurrup, Hannah!

Yet positioning herself as Westminster’s snake in the grass is not her biggest clanger, here.

No, that is the inarguable fact that what she is saying is total twaddle.



Like the mad ramblings of, dare I say, a drunken fool.

The odd drink during working hours is NOT a problem for the vast majority of the workforce, over half of whom have so-called “white collar” admin/office jobs.

Sure, you don’t want your brain surgeons necking a couple of sherbets before they step into the operating theatre.

Ditto anyone doing something that requires the absolute sharpest of focus, such as pilots or someone installing your boiler, you know, a plumber . . . like Hannah Spencer MP.

So they don’t drink and work. Good.



But you have to reason that if it is legally OK to enjoy a drink prior to getting behind the wheel of your car, you can probably handle a mildly intellectual challenge after one or two scoops.

Something like, I dunno, casting your vote on an issue you have probably thought long and hard about for many weeks, months or possibly your entire working life (or been told to back by your friendly whip).

I have written some of my best articles after washing down a lunchtime pizza with a pint of Moretti.

I can moderate my intake, you see, like most sensible people (and MPs) in Britain, many of whom do enjoy the odd working hours sherbert, Hannah, they just don’t invite fun-sponge tattletales like you.



Not every MP is throwing drinks down their neck like the late John Prescott famously did when he skulled a pint in five seconds on the campaign trail to be Labour leader in 1994 (now, there was a legend in his own lunchtime).

It might be different if it was not alcohol people were ingesting at work but something a little harder.

Like a bowl of crack, or shooting up some skag in the Commons bogs.

Some may already be doing this — we learnt last month ex-MP Crispin Blunt liked a blast of crystal meth — but more may start if the Greens get their way.

Hannah and her hemp-wearing homies want to legalise all drugs because they think that will stop the misery and shame of addiction.



Only if people behave in the way the Greens would like them too of course — which presumably means no toking from nine to five!

That may prove difficult.

I’m no neurobiologist but I do know that most drug users tend not to limit their consumption to out-of-office hours.

Spencer’s defenders claim it’s daft to draw any equivalence between drinking and doing drugs in the workplace.

No one will take drugs at work, is their confident assumption, which shows how out of touch they are with the world.



A recent survey by Bupa revealed one in three people in Britain have “used or witnessed substance abuse or addictive behaviours during work hours”.

And addiction site drugabuse.com found one in five US workers admitted to using cannabis at work.

Who cares about America? Well, they’ve legalised marijuana in 25 states.

So go figure.

Not surprisingly Spencer’s sneering has come under fire from many right honourable members.



Ale monster Nigel Farage was, of course, straight out the blocks, tweeting: “The Greens are happy to legalise heroin and crack, but now we learn they think an afternoon pint is a step too far.”

Meanwhile, Luke Charters, MP for York Outer explained: “MPs work long days for constituents, and yes, sometimes share a drink in the evening with colleagues.”

Charters, one of several Labour MPs who went on the attack, also accused Spencer and her leader, Zack Polanski, of resorting to “clickbait” politics.

We can expect more of this, because for Labour this is about more than the odd drink at work.



Party strategists know that the hard-left loonies in the Green Party represent an existential threat, one that will emerge in a technicolour rainbow after next week’s local elections.

The Greens are predicted to steal SIX councils off Labour in London alone, according to a YouGov poll last week.

So for Starmer’s shower it is a case of kill or be killed . . . or form some kind of shoddy coalition, which is already being mooted.

For the rest of us, Spencer’s ill-judged idealism is just more evidence of the kind of bats**t thinking that has captured the once environment-focused Green Party.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A window into the kind of mad world we will be forced to live in if Polanski’s crackpots make too many gains.



A bankrupt Marxist dystopia that will only ever succeed in one thing — driving us all to drink.

News.title: Vladimir Putin’s starving troops ‘are EATING each other on battlefield with sick cannibals munching on comrades’ leg’
News.content:
HORROR OF HORRORS Vladimir Putin’s starving troops ‘are EATING each other on battlefield with sick cannibals munching on comrades’ leg’

VLADIMIR Putin’s soldiers are turning to cannibalism after running low on provisions during the deep winter, it has been alleged.

Intercepted audio communications between Russian officers and photos point to “starvation” on the frontline in Ukraine, forcing comrades to eat each other.





A Ukrainian intelligence source said they had evidence of at least five such incidents, The Sunday Times reported.

Among the most disturbing incidents reportedly happened in November 2025 near the town of Myrnohrad in Donetsk region.

A Russian soldier referred to by his call sign Khromoy, meaning “limpy”, was caught after killing two comrades and attempting to eat the leg of one of them.

He is understood to have been serving with the 95th regiment of the 5th Separate Guards Motor Rifle Brigade.

In a Telegram exchange, an unnamed officer reportedly shared details of the cannibalistic act to Lieutenant Razikov Vladislav Abdulkhalykovych, deputy commander of the brigade’s reconnaissance battalion.

Abdulkhalykovych responded: “Are they not being fed or what? I don’t understand.”



The officer replied: “Ours will also soon start eating each other… All the guys are skinny. Everyone is on starvation rations.”

He also shared several images, including a graphic photo of the leg and pictures of a malnourished soldier.

AI detection tools suggested the images had not been digitally altered, the Times reported.



An independent conflict surgeon who reviewed the image of the leg said it does not look like a blast wound, adding: “It looks like it has been cut with a sharp knife.”

Describing the situation a voice message, the unnamed officer said: “In short, one ally killed two others and he tried … he cut off a leg and was already trying to eat one of them.

“In the end, today they went and found the place where he had taken them to the basement, cut off a leg and was already, through a meat grinder or something, sitting there, turning it, trying to eat …



“He opened fire on them when they came to check on him. They killed him.”

It was later revealed that the soldier was found in a basement where he had allegedly dragged the corpses.

The officer added: “They went and found the place where he had taken them to the basement, cut off a leg and was already, through a meat grinder or something, sitting there, turning it, trying to eat.”

The suspect opened fire when approached and was subsequently killed.

Two other Telegram conversations included discussion of separate cases of cannibalism.



A conversation from April 3 last year, detailed a complaint from a soldier with the call sign Most, from the 54th Motorised Rifle Regiment, who did not want to share a dugout with a Russian cannibal comrade.

“If he were a human being, he could stay here as long as he liked, but he ate a corpse, human meat,” he told his commanding officer.

“I am a Muslim. I don’t want someone like that coming into my shelter.”

Russia described the allegations as “propaganda,” saying: “What you have described are fabrications supplied by Ukrainian military intelligence – an outfit whose function is the production of propaganda, not the gathering of facts.”

While the cases appear to be isolated, this is not the first time that claims of cannibalism among Russian troops have surfaced.



This comes almost a year after a recording shared by Ukraine’s military intelligence agency (HUR) suggested that a Russian soldier lived off his fellow’s remains for two weeks.

The victim had been reported missing by his command, but it was later discovered that the cannibal had killed him for food.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Russian commander from a reconnaissance unit from the 68th Motorized Rifle Division can be heard detailing the horrors one of his subordinates.

“Nobody ran away. Brelok took him out and then ate him for two f**king weeks,” he said.

News.title: New Epstein claims as survivors allege gang rapes at remote Zorro ranch
News.content:
New Epstein claims as survivors allege gang rapes at remote Zorro ranch

SENSITIVE CONTENT Survivors have claimed in an all-new documentary that a series of nightmare acts, including gang rape, were carried out on a New Mexico ranch

View 4 Images Epstein's Zorro ranch is at the centre of new allegations (Image: AP)

Jeffrey Epstein's infamous Zorro ranch was a site for violent sex games where men were gang raped and women were strangled to death, it has been claimed.

A bombshell new documentary has included claims from survivors and witnesses about the "baby-making" ranch in New Mexico, which became the subject of an all-new criminal inquiry in February. Lawmakers in the state who launched an investigation had said they heard "very disturbing reports of some of the activity going on there", and that "horrible things" had occurred at the "isolated" property near the town of Stanley.

In a series of new testimonies, victims have shed light on the scale of the alleged depravity that occurred at the property.

Peter Mandelson probed by EU anti-fraud office in fresh blow over Epstein READ MORE :

View 4 Images Epstein is believed to have trafficked his victims around the US (Image: Corbis via Getty Images)

Victims told 60 Minutes they were taken out to the desert compound and subject to "forced on sexual rape". One brave survivor said she was trafficked across multiple Epstein properties, but said Zorro was the most terrifying of the lot, reports The Sun.

She told the programme: "The scariest was Zorro Ranch. It’s in the middle of nowhere and surrounded by mountains and miles and miles of dirt.

"There was a lot of time being in my room like a mouse in a trap waiting for a knock on the door and for someone to say, ‘Jeffrey is ready for his massage now’.” Expanding on what the massage order meant, She said it translated to: “Rape, full on, forced on sexual rape."

View 4 Images The former ranch in Santa Fe, New Mexico (Image: Getty Images)

The latest disclosures build on a previous, anonymous and unsubstantiated claim submitted to the FBI in 2019 which said two "foreign girls" had died during sex at the ranch and were buried on its grounds.

State authorities used the tip to launch new investigations this year, including a criminal case led by the New Mexico Department of Justice and "truth commission" led by the New Mexico state legislature.

View 4 Images Democrat congresswoman Melanie Stansbury has vowed to turn the Epstein files into the Epstein trials (Image: Getty Images for Women's March)

Democrat congresswoman Melanie Stansbury, who has vowed to turn the Epstein files into the "Epstein trials", said of the tip: "That particular tip … matched the pattern of other abuse and transport and trafficking of women. And that’s why it raised alarm bells for me. There’s certainly hundreds of allegations of women who experienced really dark experiences.

Article continues below

"So I think we’re really dedicated to getting to the bottom of the truth of what happened in New Mexico and on that property. They have now conducted a full investigation physically into the property including imaging all 7,500 acres of the property, they are also doing a technical analysis of the imaging data to see if it reveals anything and one of the things that was quite odd is that there were still handwritten letters, documents, and books, still at the property."

News.title: Mark Selby gets official response to 'atrocious' complaint after crashing out of World Championship
News.content:
Mark Selby gets official response to 'atrocious' complaint after crashing out of World Championship

Mark Selby was beaten by Chinese prospect Wu Yize in the World Snooker Championship on Monday – but he was not happy with the conditions at the Crucible

View 2 Images Mark Selby has been given a response by the WST (Image: (Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images))

Mark Selby criticised the 'horrific' state of the Crucible table after crashing out of the World Championship in a 13-11 defeat to China’s Wu Yize. Four-time champion Selby drew on his years of experience to push the 22-year-old rising star all the way but ultimately cut a frustrated figure as Wu held his nerve to book his place in the last eight.

‌



The 22-year-old Chinese star overcame him 13-11 to reach the quarter-finals at the Crucible. Selby did win two frames in a row towards the end to move from 12-9 down to 12-11, but a scrappy final frame but both players ended with Wu getting himself over the line.

‌



Selby paid homage to his younger opponent and admitted he was far from his best. But when it came to himself and the conditions at the Crucible, he said: "I felt like I only played well really in the first session. I played good in the first session, then after that I just missed ball-after-ball.

‌



"Wu's long game was good, I felt like his safety was good but neither of us really scored that well. Just too many silly errors really. Whether it was a lapse in concentration, I am not sure, I felt like the conditions were atrocious really in both matches.

"The cushions were really bouncing. The table got re-covered last night and I felt like it played no better than the other sessions. That is no excuse, I still missed silly balls and didn't deserve to win, really."

A World Snooker Tour spokesperson said in response: “There are always challenges in providing the best possible conditions for players as there are many factors which affect this.

“Our dedicated team of table-fitters work tirelessly in delivering the best possible conditions and they are constantly monitoring the tables. We have systems in place where players can give feedback after every match.”

View 2 Images Mark Selby during his match against Wu Yize at the World Snooker Championship (Image: (Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images))

‌



On Yize, Selby said: “He’s great for our game, he’s great to watch and very, very attacking. Some of the balls he took on against me, I’m not sure they were the right shot, but they were going in. He’s still young and loving the game.

“I think he’s a world champion in the making. Who knows? It could be this year, but I do think he’ll probably win it at some stage.

“I don’t think he played great in that match but some of the standards he plays to when he gets on a bit of a run, he’s hard to stop.”

News.title: Inside the White House ring of steel ahead of King Charles's visit
News.content:
Inside the White House ring of steel ahead of King Charles's visit

A Mirror reporter walked the nearly two-mile security perimeter around the White House as Washington ramps up protection following an alleged assassination attempt on Donald Trump – just as King Charles III and Queen Camilla prepare for their state visit.

View 4 Images Urgent wall of steel built to block off White House amid panic ahead of King's visit (Image: Jack Hobbs)

In the days following a suspected third assassination attempt on President Donald Trump, security across the nation's capital has been ramped up considerably.

‌



The Mirror US paid a visit to the country's most significant building just one day after Cole Tomas Allen allegedly tried to gain entry to a White House Correspondents' dinner where the president was in attendance, reportedly armed with a shotgun, handgun and knives.

‌



During a walk along the nearly 2-mile-long security perimeter on Monday morning, it was abundantly clear that the forthcoming visit of King Charles III and Queen Camilla is being treated with the utmost seriousness. Members of the National Guard and the Metropolitan Police were noticeably more active than normal, patrolling the area surrounding the executive complex and the White House.

‌



There was also a heightened presence of Secret Service agents posted at several entrances to government buildings, with others positioned in police vehicles on the street and across various driveways. Frustrated tourists found themselves struggling to catch an unobstructed glimpse of the White House, as the surrounding area is now dominated by a towering, unscalable metal fence, reports the Mirror US.

View 4 Images I managed to walk the entire security perimeter of the White House ahead of the state visit by King Charles and Queen Camilla (Image: Jack Hobbs)

King Charles meets Donald Trump LIVE: Royals lands in US to ring of steel after shooting READ MORE :

OPINION Russell Myers in Washington DC 'Trump hysteria won't bother Charles or Camilla - they'll keep calm and carry on'

‌



I overheard one family squabbling over where to find the best vantage point for a photograph, as the fence stretches the entire length of 14th Street and 17th Street.

It wasn't long before they made their way over to me, asking whether I knew of anywhere they could get a clear, unobstructed view. The security arrangements also appeared to frustrate another couple, who began rowing after finding that The Ellipse, located just beyond the standard White House boundary fence and normally accessible to visitors, had been shut for the state visit.

"I can't believe that it's closed," the man complained, visibly annoyed that his usual walking path had been temporarily blocked off. "Well, what would you like me to do? Tell the guards to open it up for us? It will reopen tomorrow," his partner retorted sharply.

‌



View 4 Images Charles and Camilla will spend four days in the US (Image: Jack Hobbs)

The Ellipse and its vicinity are unlikely to reopen the following day, as the King and Queen will stay in Washington until Wednesday, when the president and first lady will hold a banquet in their honour. The continuation of the King and Queen's visit has been cast into uncertainty following the shooting incident occurring in such close proximity to their arrival.

Nevertheless, on Sunday, Buckingham Palace confirmed that the visit would proceed as scheduled, and while security measures have been implemented, the streets have been decorated with American and British flags to mark the occasion. "The King and Queen are most grateful to all those who have worked at pace to ensure this remains the case and are looking forward to the visit getting underway tomorrow," a palace statement declared.

Article continues below

View 4 Images (Image: Jack Hobbs)

The UK ambassador to the US, Christian Turner, confirmed on Sunday that he was "very confident that their Majesties will have the very best security throughout the visit." Charles and Camilla are due to be welcomed by President Trump and First Lady Melania at approximately 4:15pm at the White House's south portico.

The heads of state will gather for a private afternoon tea in the Green Room on the State floor. The King and Queen will also be given a tour of the beehives situated on the South Lawn, coming just a week after the first lady revealed that the White House had extended its longstanding honey-production programme, which includes a new beehive modelled after the White House itself.

News.title: Plane crashes and erupts in flames killing at least 14 in South Sudan
News.content:
Plane crashes and erupts in flames killing at least 14 in South Sudan

A plane has crashed and burst into flames on the outskirts of South Sudan’s capital Juba, killing all 13 passengers and the pilot, the civil aviation authority said

View 3 Images The plane crashed into a ball of flames on the ground (Image: AP)

At least 14 people have been killed after a plane crashed and burst into flames in poor weather.

‌



The Cessna aircraft went down on the outskirts of South Sudan’s capital, killing all 13 passengers and the pilot, the civil aviation authority said.

‌



Preliminary reports indicate that the plane arriving from Yei town may have crashed due to weather conditions that caused poor visibility. The civil aviation authority said the dead included two Kenyans, and the rest were South Sudanese.

‌



View 3 Images The plane seen smouldering on the ground (Image: AP)

Donald Trump calls for Jimmy Kimmel to be FIRED after Melania joke READ MORE :

The authority said a team was dispatched to the site about 12 miles outside Juba. The Cessna 208 Caravan, which was operated by CityLink Aviation, ‌lost communication while flying from Yei to Juba International Airport.

Air traffic control is understood to have lost contact with the plane after 30 minutes into the journey which would have been a distance of around 80 miles.

‌



Videos of the crash site shared on social media showed remains of the aircraft in flames with the location shown appeared hilly and misty. “All the bodies were charred beyond recognition,” reportedly said a member of a UN rescue team that was sent to the scene.

View 3 Images Authorities said 14 people had died in the tragedy (Image: AP)

Meanwhile, a US politician and a pilot were tragically killed in a fireball plane crash last weekend. Liz Conmy, a North Dakota state legislator, died after the plane went down in a suburban park shortly after take-off.

Article continues below

The plane was seen plummeting down before exploding into flames. Emergency services raced to the small park to find the wreckage engulfed in flames. It’s understood the plane had just left Crystal Airport on Saturday morning when it plunged down into a green space in Brooklyn Park, north of Minneapolis.

The North Dakota Democratic–Nonpartisan League Party, an affiliate of the national Democratic Party, confirmed Conmy’s death in a social media post, calling her a champion for public education, the environment, and transparency.

“We are completely heartbroken and gutted by the loss of Representative Liz Conmy. Her death is a profound loss for our state,” the party said in a post on X. Officers responded to a report of a small airplane crash at 11:51am and found an aircraft that had crashed and caught fire in a park in the city of Brooklyn Park, Minnesota, shortly after taking off, Brooklyn Park Police Inspector Matt Rabe said.

News.title: Moment dad FAINTS on hospital floor while watching his wife in labour
News.content:
Moment dad FAINTS on hospital floor while watching his wife in labour

Maicon Pedroso briefly lost consciousness as his wife delivered their second child - with medics seen in a video of the delivery lowering him to the hospital floor

Dad faints during labour shock

A dad overcome by the birth of his second child was captured on camera fainting in the delivery room as his newborn arrived via C-section.

‌



Maicon Pedroso collapsed at a hospital in Criciúma, Brazil, while witnessing his wife, Mariane Felippe, deliver his second daughter during C-section labour on April 18. An attending medic dressed in scrubs was forced to grab the dad, who was clutching Ms Felippe's hand the second his daughter was delivered, by the armpits and steady him.

‌



He was gently lowered to the floor, where he was placed, unconscious. Maicon, who woke a short time after the fainting incident, said he regained consciousness in hospital with no memory of his child being born.

‌



Donald Trump calls for Jimmy Kimmel to be FIRED after Melania joke READ MORE :

Horror teen who killed two in first school shooting now incarcerated fork lift truck driver READ MORE :

View 3 Images Maicon Pedroso fainted as his wife delivered a baby via C-section (Image: Jam Press/Matre Fotografia)

Maicon told local media: "I don't remember anything at all from the moment the baby was born." He and his wife called the hospital in the early hours of the morning last week as Ms Felippe's water broke. Doctors decided to give the mum a C-section, which went smoothly up until the final moment.

Patricia Vogel and Viviane Borges, two photographers attending the delivery, remarked on how well the process appeared to have been before "the exact moment the baby was born".

‌



They said: "When we arrived, they were a bit anxious, but everything was going as expected. It was all happening in a light, calm way, with the medical team feeling very confident and the parents too. Then, at 8.24am, at the exact moment the baby was born, the father fainted."

View 3 Images The dad was lain on the hospital floor

The pair, who together have "documented more than 1,500 births", they told local media, added they had seen men faint at the scene previously.

‌



They said: "We've been exclusively dedicated to birth photography for five years. We've documented more than 1,500 births, and this is definitely a scene we've seen happen a few times before." Medics, on the other hand, were said to have been taken by surprise after the dad lost consciousness.

While the fainting came as a shock, the dad was said to have quite quickly recovered and was able to spend time with his newborn following the C-section.

View 3 Images The dad fainted as his wife delivered their second baby (Image: Jam Press/Matre Fotografia)

Article continues below

The dad's delivery reaction was captured in a clip and shared online - where it has since racked up nearly 19 million views and courted a series of comments from onlookers. Many viewers were keen to point out the dad's reaction in the face of his wife's delivery of a newborn child.

They said: "Women don't realise how tough it can be for the father. Stay strong, warrior!" Another joked that the dad was "stealing the spotlight".

A third viewer offered a window into the wife's perspective, saying: "Imagine having seven layers of skin cut away and your husband saying in the background, "But I had it worse because I fainted."'

News.title: Suspect shooter charged with attempting to assassinate Donald Trump at White House
News.content:
Suspect shooter charged with attempting to assassinate Donald Trump at White House

Cole Tomas Allen was taken into custody after the shooting on Saturday night and he has now been charged with attempting to assassinate Donald Trump at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner

View 4 Images Cole Tomas Allen was taken into custody after the shooting (Image: FACEBOOK)

A man who allegedly tried to storm the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner with guns and knives has been charged with attempting to assassinate Donald Trump.

‌



Cole Tomas Allen was taken into custody after the shooting on Saturday night and is being charged in federal court in Washington.

‌



He appeared in court Monday to face charges in a chaotic encounter that resulted in shots being fired, Trump being rushed off the stage and guests ducking for cover underneath their tables.

‌



Authorities say an officer wearing a bullet-resistant vest was shot in the vest but is expected to recover.

View 4 Images A court sketch of Cole Tomas Allen (Image: AP)

Donald Trump calls for Jimmy Kimmel to be FIRED after Melania joke READ MORE :

Allen, of Torrance, California, is being represented by lawyers with the federal defender's office and sat beside them in court in a blue jail uniform. He also was charged with transport of a firearm and ammunition in interstate commerce and with discharging a firearm during a crime of violence. He did not enter a plea.

‌



Prosecutors have not revealed a motive, but in a message that authorities say was sent by Allen to family members minutes before the attack, Allen referred to himself as a "Friendly Federal Assassin," made repeated references to the Republican president without naming him and alluded to grievances over a range of Trump administration actions.

View 4 Images Cole Tomas Allen on the ground after being stopped by law enforcement (Image: @REALDONALDTRUMP / TRUTH SOCIAL/AFP via Getty Images)

Investigators are treating the writings, along with a trail of social media posts and interviews with family members, as some of the clearest evidence of the suspect's mindset and possible motives.

‌



Allen, 31, is believed to have travelled by train from California to Chicago and then onto Washington, where he checked himself in as a guest at the hotel where the gala dinner was held with its typically tight security, acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said.

View 4 Images The Trumps pictured as the shooting unfolded at the hotel (Image: Pixel8000)

Video posted by Trump shows a man, who authorities say was armed with guns and knives, running past a security barricade as Secret Service agents run towards him and managed to bring him to the ground.

Article continues below

Police have previously said that the suspect was a guest at the Washington Hilton where the dinner was being held and they believe he acted alone.

Records show Allen is a highly educated tutor and amateur video game developer. A social media profile for a man with the same name and a photo that appears to match that of the suspect show he worked part-time for the last six years at a company that offers admissions counselling and test preparation services to aspiring college students.

News.title: Donald Trump calls for Jimmy Kimmel to be FIRED after Melania joke
News.content:
Donald Trump calls for Jimmy Kimmel to be FIRED after Melania joke

US President Donald Trump has blasted comic Jimmy Kimmel on social media after he joked that Melania Trump had a glow of an “expectant widow” saying he should be fired

View 3 Images (Image: ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA)

Donald Trump has hit out at a Jimmy Kimmel gag where he joked that Melania Trump had the glow of an “expectant widow".

‌



The comic made the comments in an episode of Jimmy Kimmel Live last Thursday before a shooting during the White House Correspondents' Dinner on Saturday night.

‌



"Our First Lady, Melania, is here. Look at Melania, so beautiful. Mrs Trump, you have a glow like an expectant widow," Kimmel said.

‌



And now Trump wrote on Truth Social saying that Kimmel should be sacked over the comments which is the latest incident in a long running feud. Trump previously celebrated Kimmel being suspended by the network ABC for a monologue referencing the shooting of Charlie Kirk where he compared the US President's grief to “how a 4-year-old mourns a goldfish”.

View 3 Images The Trumps pictured as the shooting unfolded at the hotel (Image: Pixel8000)

Trump now said on social media: "Wow, Jimmy Kimmel, who is in no way funny as attested to by his terrible Television Ratings, made a statement on his Show that is really shocking. He showed a fake video of the First Lady, Melania, and our son, Barron, like they were actually sitting in his studio, listening to him speak, which they weren’t, and never would be.

‌



"He then stated, “Our First Lady, Melania, is here. Look at Melania, so beautiful. Mrs. Trump, you have a glow like an expectant widow." A day later a lunatic tried entering the ballroom of the White House Correspondents Dinner, loaded up with a shotgun, handgun, and many knives. He was there for a very obvious and sinister reason.

View 3 Images Jimmy Kimmel said that Melania Trump had the glow of an "expectant widow" (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"I appreciate that so many people are incensed by Kimmel’s despicable call to violence, and normally would not be responsive to anything that he said but, this is something far beyond the pale. Jimmy Kimmel should be immediately fired by Disney and ABC. Thank you for your attention to this matter! President DONALD J. TRUMP."

‌



Cole Tomas Allen, 31, from Torrance, California, is the suspected gunman who was allegedly armed with guns and knives when he stormed the Washington Hilton on Saturday night.

Melania earlier today also urged the ABC network to "take a stand" over Kimmel and his show. In a post on X, the first lady said: "Kimmel’s hateful and violent rhetoric is intended to divide our country. His monologue about my family isn’t comedy- his words are corrosive and deepens the political sickness within America. People like Kimmel shouldn’t have the opportunity to enter our homes each evening to spread hate.

" A coward, Kimmel hides behind ABC because he knows the network will keep running cover to protect him. Enough is enough. It is time for ABC to take a stand. How many times will ABC’s leadership enable Kimmel’s atrocious behavior at the expense of our community."

News.title: 'Trump hysteria won't bother Charles or Camilla - they'll keep calm and carry on'
News.content:
'Trump hysteria won't bother Charles or Camilla - they'll keep calm and carry on'

The Mirror's royal editor Russell Myers is in Washington DC for Charles' controversial state visit, and believes his sense of duty to the monarchy will overpower the frenzy around his Stateside trip

View 4 Images The King with Trump at Windsor Castle (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

For all the hysteria surrounding the royal visit to the United States of America, there are two people who will take it in their stride - our King and Queen. This is the King’s 20th official visit to US and he is well versed in dealing with the often turbulent nature of this country.

‌



Last minute security arrangements put in place to safeguard Charles and Camilla following Saturday's mayhem in Washington have resulted in a ring of steel being put round the royals. But for the King and Queen it’s very much a case of ‘keep calm and carry on’.

‌



View 4 Images The King with US president Donald Trump (Image: PA)

‌



While a chorus of discontent surrounding this controversial trip has grown in recent weeks, against a backdrop of President Trump’s war in the Middle East and arguments over tariffs and even the Falkland Islands, the visit has been years in the planning.

Buckingham Palace earmarked the 250th anniversary of US independence in the King’s diary long ago and now more than ever, the monarch is intent on honouring this side of his public duty.

Last year, Charles clocked up more engagements at home and abroad than any other member of the royal family. Despite living with cancer for more than two years, he has carried on at a relentless pace, which shows no sign of slowing down.

‌



View 4 Images King Charles with Donald Trump at Windsor Castle last year (Image: AP)

He is acutely aware of his age, the requirements made to live with his condition and the time available to him to cement a legacy as sovereign befitting a life in public service.

On the face of it, the King and Trump could not be more different.

‌



The two men vary wildly on discourse, honesty, integrity, global cohesion, the environment - I could go on.

View 4 Images The King will spend two days with Trump in Washington DC (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Yet, as we clearly saw when the King and Queen hosted the President and the First Lady, there is a reverence reserved for very few people, let alone world leaders.

Article continues below

The real proof will be if Trump dials down his disgraceful threats to Britain as a result of the King deploying all the diplomacy needed to fill the cracks in the so-called special relationship.

News.title: How Kenya's Sabastian Sawe broke the two-hour barrier at London Marathon
News.content:
Sabastian Sawe has always had a propensity to surprise.

Having never competed on the road, the Kenyan began the 2022 Seville half marathon as a pacemaker, proceeded to drop everybody within the first 10km, and carried on to claim victory in a course record time.

Running the second-fastest marathon debut in history in Valencia in 2024, Sawe again hinted at his potential.

That time of two hours two minutes five seconds was only 12 seconds slower than the late Kelvin Kiptum's first marathon two years earlier, before Kiptum went on to break the world record in Chicago in 2023.

There were signs.

But they were far from sufficient to prepare anyone for the momentous occasion which unfolded on a perfect April morning in London on Sunday.

Sporting immortality, secured in 1:59:30.

Speaking to BBC Sport 24 hours after making history as the first person to run a sub-two-hour marathon in a competitive race, Sawe said the time came as a surprise even to him, with his focus primarily on retaining his title.

"It was not in my mind. I was well prepared for this year's London Marathon, but what comes surprised me because I was not thinking to run a world record."

But Sawe, 31, says he can go even faster.

"It was possible to run faster yesterday," he said. "Even 1:58 is possible."

Sawe, born in Kenya's Rift Valley, where his father worked as a maize farmer, declared it "a day to remember" after obliterating Kiptum's world record by 65 seconds.

Others searched for the words to pay appropriate tribute to an accomplishment once considered impossible.

"Nobody thought that a sub-two-hour marathon under World Athletics conditions would be done in their lifetime," London Marathon race director Hugh Brasher told BBC Sport.

"This is an unbelievable day for sport. It is sport and history in the making."

Former women's marathon world record holder Paula Radcliffe said: "We've witnessed history being made, but it is more than that.

"It is an iconic barrier that there has been this discussion over for a long time about whether it is even possible."

The Trump administration has purged more than 100 immigration judges and hired more than 140 in their place, but many have no relevant legal experience in the field, according to a report.

In a bid to carry out the largest deportation campaign in U.S. history, as set out by President Donald Trump when he returned to office, the Justice Department replaced many immigration judges hired under the Biden administration with a more “malleable workforce,” a former appointee told The Washington Post.

There are approximately 700 immigration judges handling over 3 million cases across the country—and they work for Trump’s Justice Department, and are not part of the judicial branch. They are responsible for deciding whether undocumented migrants should be granted asylum and be allowed to remain in the country, or whether they should be deported.

Many immigration judges quit or retired when Trump returned to the White House, in addition to the more than 100 the Justice Department fired, according to the Post.

The new hires include an attorney who has represented three Jan. 6 rioters and a Minnesota-based attorney who asked what could be done to support the Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers amid the crackdown in Minneapolis, where two American citizens were killed by federal agents.

open image in gallery The Trump administration has purged more than 100 immigration judges and hired more than 140 in their place, but many have no relevant legal experience in the field, according to a report ( AFP/Getty )

Kerry Doyle told the outlet that she was hired under Biden to serve as an immigration judge but was then fired last year before she heard any cases. “They’re trying to create a malleable workforce that will do what they want without question,” Doyle, a former ICE official, told the outlet. “That’s what I think the goal is.”

Two-thirds of the new hires, who will be paid between $159,951 to $207,500 per year, have no relevant legal immigration experience listed in their biographies, according to the Post’s analysis of announcements by the Justice Department. Only 24 percent of them had worked for ICE, the immigration courts, or for the Department of Homeland Security.

The National Association of Immigration Judges told the outlet that the usual training for new appointees has been cut from five weeks to three.

The Independent has contacted the Justice Department for comment.

Under the second Trump administration, the immigration courts have been overhauled, largely overseen by deputy White House chief of staff Stephen Miller.

The Justice Department’s Board of Immigration Appeals has reportedly ushered in new orders for judges to dismiss cases on the request of the federal government so that defendants can be arrested. Judges have also been advised to grant asylum “more sparingly,” according to the newspaper.

open image in gallery There are approximately 700 immigration judges handling over three million cases across the country—and they work for Trump’s Justice Department, and are not part of the judicial branch ( AFP/Getty )

Eyebrows have been raised at some of the appointments, which the Justice Department has been recruiting for in social media posts.

Melissa Isaak, an Army veteran, was named a temporary immigration judge in Atlanta, Georgia, this month. Isaak defended three Jan. 6 rioters accused of storming the Capitol after Trump lost the 2020 election, but she later withdrew from two of the cases, according to the Post. Isaak also falsely claimed that statistics show more men are victims of domestic abuse than women.

Another recruit appointed this month was Minnesota-based lawyer Nathan M. Hansen, who reportedly shared social media posts about the “Haitian invasion of Ohio,” as peddled by Trump and Vice President JD Vance during the 2024 presidential campaign. Hansen has promoted other conspiracy theories, including “Pizzagate,” which baselessly alleged Democrats were running a child sex trafficking ring out of a Washington, D.C. pizzeria, according to the newspaper.

In a recent news release, the Justice Department’s Executive Office for Immigration Review agency touted the new appointees.

“EOIR remains committed to reducing the immigration court backlog and unwinding the policies of the Biden Administration that included a de facto open border and amnesty,” said the agency’s director, Daren K. Margolin. “These new highly qualified immigration judges have sworn to decide the cases before them based on the law — that is, the laws passed by the United States Congress.”

The gunman who tried to storm into the annual White House Correspondents' Association dinner exposed gaps that need to be closed to prevent future attacks, former Secret Service agents say.

"The system worked. Could it be much better? Yes," Bobby McDonald, who protected then-presidents Bill Clinton and George W. Bush, told The Independent on Monday. "We had a positive outcome, not a successful one."

With President Donald Trump insisting that the event be rescheduled "within 30 days," McDonald said the the Secret Service would have to quickly develop ideas to beef up security.

"I think they have to have some discussions about creativity," he said. "They're going to have to blow up their plan."

In a prepared statement, Secret Service spokesperson Anthony Guglielmi said, "While the protective model for White House Correspondents’ Dinner event proved effective, the key takeaway for future events is that enhancements should be expected at every level, as that is how the model is designed to function."

open image in gallery Ex-Secret Service agents say the attempted attack on the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner exposed gaps in security ( Getty )

"Every protective decision is driven by intelligence amid a dynamic and currently elevated threat environment. We are actively focused on identifying the trigger for this incident and fully understanding the factors that led to it," Guglielmi said.

The White House didn't immediately return a request for comment but Trump, who on Saturday made his first appearance at the annual event , has praised the Secret Service and other law enforcement officers for acting "quickly and bravely" and doing a "fantastic job."

Cole Tomas Allen, 31, of Torrance, California, was reportedly armed with a shotgun, a handgun and several knives when he allegedly barreled past a checkpoint before being stopped from entering the ballroom in the Washington Hilton hotel where the dinner was taking place.

The hotel is the same one where then-president Ronald Reagan was wounded in a 1981 shooting outside as he walked toward his limousine after delivering a speech.

Allen reportedly checked into the hotel on Friday after traveling across the country by train and allegedly sent relatives a manifesto where he marveled that security efforts seemed focused "outside" and that “not a single person there considers the possibility that I could be a threat.”

open image in gallery Cole Tomas Allen is seen in custody after allegedly attempting to storm the White House Correspondents’ Association Dinner while armed with guns and knives ( Reuters )

“What the hell is the Secret Service doing?” he wrote. “Like, I expected security cameras at every bend, bugged hotel rooms, armed agents every 10 feet, metal detectors out the wazoo. What I got (who knows, maybe they’re pranking me!) is nothing."

Secret Service Director Sean Curran has said that since Allen was unable to barge into the ballroom, it "shows that our multi-layered protection works."

Former Secret Service Agent Bill Gage, who said he was "at the Hilton all the time" during 5 1/2 years assigned to the Washington, D.C., field office, described the agency's protective model as "concentric and overlapping lawyers of security."

The decades-old protocols start with emptying an event space, posting agents at every entrance and exit, using specially trained dogs to sweep the area for explosives and setting up metal-detecting magnetometers to screen guests for weapons, he said.

"The big takeaway is the protective model worked," said Gage, now director of executive protection for the SafeHaven Security Group. "He got past the magnetometer but he didn't get to the next layer."

The Washington Hilton has more than 1,100 rooms and the WHCA dinner reportedly drew about 2,300 guests to its underground ballroom, which Gage said presented a series of security challenges.

"It is incredibly difficult for the Secret Service to secure a very busy hotel on a very busy street," he said.

open image in gallery Journalists report outside the Washington Hilton hotel one day after an attempted attack inside against the annual White House Correspondents' Association dinner ( Getty )

Gage likened Saturday night's incident to the two previous assassination attempts against Trump, calling them all "low-tech attacks by people with no training."

He also said there was probably "nothing to be done" that would have allowed authorities to identify Cole as a potential threat beforehand.

"There were no tripwires for this guy that he was setting off along the way, except for about an hour before the attack he sent a manifesto to his family," Gage said. "We're a free country. We don't keep tabs on our citizens. This isn't China."

McDonald, who retired as assistant special agent in charge in charge of then-vice president Joe Biden's security detail, said he thought there were "numerous things that could have been done" to further safeguard the ballroom.

"Had he seen more security in the lobby or at the magnetometer, he might have turned around," McDonald said of Allen.

McDonald also said the Secret Service needed to create "better time and space distance" between checkpoints, and both he and Gage said the agency would likely consider setting up serpentine barriers before the magnetometers.

McDonald, now an assistant professor of criminal justice and criminology at the University of New Haven, also said that the agency “has to look at the possibility of setting up its security perimeter earlier, as well as equipping agents with ballistic shields.

"If he was wearing a suicide vest instead of the weapons he was carrying, we could have had a very different outcome," he said of the attacker.

McDonald noted that "in a lot of different countries, you stand on line for a lot of different things."

"At many hotels in many countries you have to go through a security check before you drive in," he said. "We have to finally accept the fact that we have to be more accepting of a delay before getting into a hotel because you have to go through some sort of security element."

News.title: Trump pivots from ‘speech of love’ to ‘you’re a disgrace’ in 24-hour media whiplash after correspondents’ dinner shooting
News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. Over the course of American history, a few undelivered presidential speeches have taken on iconic status in the decades after they were supposed to have been given.

There’s the address John F. Kennedy would have delivered in defense of American soft power as a bulwark against communism and authoritarian threats, in which he would have declared that there was “no better form of investment in our national security” than foreign aid and warned that American leadership was dependent on global “respect for our mission in the world.”

There was Richard Nixon’s planned address to the nation in the event that Apollo 11’s lunar module engine failed to light, stranding astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin — “the men who went to the moon to explore in peace” — to “stay on the moon to rest in peace.”

And of course, there’s the “speech of love” to the American news media that Donald Trump says he would have delivered had Saturday’s White House Correspondents Dinner been allowed to resume after a gunman attempted to sprint through layers of security in a failed attempt to assassinate the president and the senior officials who were scattered around the cavernous ballroom at the Washington, D.C. Hilton.

In the run-up to the weekend’s marquee event — an annual fundraiser for scholarships administered by the White House Correspondents Association — media critics and political pundits spilled what would have probably been hundreds of gallons of ink in a pre-digital era on the propriety of the press breaking bread with a man who has spent years demonizing them as “the enemy of the people.”

open image in gallery President Donald Trump (pictured on the dais with first lady Melania and White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt before the shooting began) wanted to return to the event after with a ‘speech of love’ for the press. ( Reuters )

Would Trump use the open microphone before a captive audience of his longtime adversaries to go on the attack at a dinner meant as a celebration of the First Amendment?

It was a good question — one Trump was more than willing to answer at what became probably the only Black Tie news conference in White House history. He told reporters he “was all set to really rip it” until the shooting, after which he mused that his planned remarks would’ve been “the most inappropriate speech ever made.”

He even offered some praise for the thousands of journalists (your correspondent included) who’d endured the horrific events, remarking that he’d seen “a room that was just totally unified” in the wake of the attempted shooting.

A day later, he told Fox News that during the brief time he was pushing to continue on with the program before Secret Service forced him to return to the White House, he tasked his aides with writing replacement remarks, what he called “a speech of love.”

“But I didn’t get a chance to do that,” he added.

He later told CBS News’ 60 Minutes something similar when he described pushing to remain at the venue over his bodyguards’ objections, telling correspondent Norah O’Donnell: “I would have had to just get up and say, ‘I love you all.’ And there was love in the room. It was amazing. There was love in the room.”

open image in gallery Donald Trump speaks to Norah O'Donnell for 60 Minutes Sunday night who he would berate as ‘horrible’ in the same interview ( 60 Minutes )

But whatever goodwill he had briefly felt towards the country’s news media and the First Amendment that allows it to operate freely appeared to vanish in an instant hours later, when he sat for what he might have expected to be a softball interview with O’Donnell.

Although the network that was once home to Edward R. Murrow, Walter Cronkite and Dan Rather has undergone a decidedly pro-Trump makeover since it was purchased by billionaire David Ellison last year, under the stewardship of former New York Times conservative opinion journalist Bari Weiss, O’Donnell didn’t go to work to throw softballs on Sunday.

Instead, she asked him to respond to the words written by his would-be assassin, who allegedly wrote that he was “no longer willing to permit a pedophile, rapist, and traitor to coat my hands with his crimes” in a manifesto sent to family members just before the attempted shooting.

Trump’s reaction? Predictable.

Less than a day after he could have well been shot, he threw away talk of “unity” and went after the messenger.

“Well, I was waiting for you to read that because I knew you would because you're-- you're he-- you're horrible people,” he said as he launched into one of the most surreal presidential soliloquies in the history of the long-running program.

“I'm not a pedophile. Excuse me. Excuse me. I'm not a pedophile … I got associated with all-- stuff that has nothing to do with me. I was totally exonerated. Your friends on the other side of the plate are the ones that were involved with, little's say, Epstein or other things,” he said.

“You shouldn't be reading that on 60 Minutes. You're a disgrace. But go ahead. Let's finish the interview.”

If there was ever a post-shooting honeymoon between Trump and the press, it was over at that moment.

Within a day, he, his wife, and his top spokesperson were back to the usual things, blaming Democrats for the shooting attempt and calling for ABC to fire Jimmy Kimmel — again — because of a joke he’d told about First Lady Melania Trump days before the shooting.

And now that Trump has repeatedly called for the White House Correspondents’ Association to reschedule and re-run the dinner, there can be no question about his motives for attending this time around.

OpenAI boss Sam Altman has updated his company’s mission statement, outlining the steps needed to achieve human-level artificial intelligence.

The 1,100-word document, published on OpenAI’s website on Sunday, details five guiding “principles” to ensure artificial general intelligence (AGI) “benefits all of humanity”.

They include democratisation of the technology, greater user empowerment, improved safety resilience, better corporate adaptability, and what Altman refers to as “universal prosperity” through the building of huge amounts of AI infrastructure.

“Power in the future can either be held by a small handful of companies using and controlling superintelligence, or it can be held in a decentralised way by people,” he wrote.

“We believe the latter is much better, and our goal is to put truly general AI in the hands of as many people as possible... Our mission is to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity.”

There are some notable key differences to the language used compared to previous mission statements, which focused on ushering AGI in the safest way possible.

He claimed that holding back models that might pose a threat – like OpenAI did with the restricted roll out of GPT-2 – was a “misplaced worry”.

Instead, Altman said OpenAI would “embrace that uncertainty” by deploying its systems and learning from their interactions with the world.

OpenAI unveiled its most powerful AI model to date last week, describing it as a “new class of intelligence”.

The GPT-5.5 is designed to carry out tasks, like online research and data analysis, without human oversight.

“What’s really special about this model is how much more it can do with less guidance,” said OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman, claiming it could conduct “messy, multi-part tasks” intuitively and independently.

Early users of the latest model, which is currently only available to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users, have claimed that it feels like it is approaching human-level artificial intelligence, or artificial general intelligence (AGI).

Pietro Schirano, chief executive of AI design took MagicPath, said in a post to X that he had his “first taste of AGI” using GPT-5.5.
